If a user account might have been created by an attacker, disable the account. Don't
delete the account unless there are no plans to perform security forensics for the incident.
Isolate any known attacker control points inside the enterprise from the Internet.
Remove the malware from the affected devices.
Run a full, current antivirus scan on all suspected computers and devices to detect and
remove the payload that is associated with the ransomware.
Don't forget to scan devices that synchronize data or the targets of mapped network
drives.
Recover files on a cleaned device.
You can use File History
in Windows 11, Windows 10, Windows 8.1, and System
Protection in Windows 7 to attempt to recover your local files and folders.
Recover files in OneDrive for Business.
Files Restore in OneDrive for Business allows you to restore an entire OneDrive to a
previous point in time within the last 30 days. For more information, see Restore your
OneDrive
.
Recover deleted email.
In the rare case that the ransomware deleted all the email in a mailbox, you can recover
the deleted items. See Recover deleted messages in a user's mailbox in Exchange Online.
